title: Power-series polynomial normalization with finite fraction-field extension
statement: Let $p$ be prime, $B$ a characteristic-$p$ domain, and $M$ its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $R_0$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring complete for its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], with $B$ a finite type $R_0$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. There exist a subring $C\subset B$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and integers $n,m\geq0$, such that $B$ is finite type over $C$ and $C$ is isomorphic to the polynomial ring $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]][y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. There is a fraction field $K$ of $C$ and an embedding $K\to M$ extending $C\hookrightarrow B\hookrightarrow M$ such that $M/K$ is a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension].

proof.text: Replace R0 by its image R in B, isomorphic to R0 modulo the prime kernel. The quotient is proper, Noetherian, local and complete. Transfer these properties across the quotient-range ring equivalence. Finite type descends from R0 to its image by the finite-type ring-map composition criterion.

Apply the complete-local-domain regular-subring theorem to R. Its subring S has characteristic p. Exclude the Cohen-ring case: if its prime integer q were not divisible by p it would be a unit in characteristic p, contrary to membership in the maximal ideal. If p divides q then q=0, making the maximal ideal zero, contrary to the discrete valuation ring not being a field. Hence S is a power series ring over a field k, and its coefficient-field embedding gives characteristic p for k. Since R is finite over S and B finite type over R, B is finite type over S.

Apply normalization to the injective S-to-B map. The range C of the injective polynomial evaluation is a polynomial ring over S, contains S, and is contained in a subalgebra B0 finite over C. B0[1/g] maps bijectively to B[1/g] for nonzero g in S. The finite S-algebra generators of B still generate over C.

Surjectivity after inverting g gives, for every b in B, an element b0 in B0 and j with b0=g^j*b. For a fraction a/b in M, choose a0=g^i*a and b0=g^j*b in B0; then a/b=(a0*g^j)/(b0*g^i). The denominator is nonzero since B is a domain and g,b are nonzero. This proves M is also the fraction field of B0. Finiteness of B0 over C gives integrality, hence algebraicity of M over C and over K=Frac(C). Because B is finite type over C and M is a localization of B, M is essentially finite type over C, hence over K. An algebraic essentially finite type field extension is finite-dimensional (Mathlib Algebra.finite_of_essFiniteType_of_isAlgebraic). Equip K-to-M with FractionRing.liftAlgebra; the lift has the required scalar tower.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_powerSeries_polynomial_normalization
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [CharP B p]
    (M : Type v) [Field M] [Algebra B M] [IsFractionRing B M]
    (R₀ : Type w) [CommRing R₀] [IsNoetherianRing R₀] [IsLocalRing R₀]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R₀) R₀]
    [Algebra R₀ B] [Algebra.FiniteType R₀ B] :
    ∃ C : Subring B, Algebra.FiniteType C B ∧
      ∃ (k : Type u) (hk : Field k), letI := hk
        ∃ n m : ℕ, CharP k p ∧
          Nonempty (C ≃+* MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k)) ∧
          ∃ (K : Type u) (hK : Field K), letI := hK
            ∃ aCK : Algebra C K, letI := aCK
              ∃ hfrac : IsFractionRing C K, letI := hfrac
                ∃ aKM : Algebra K M, letI := aKM
                  letI : Algebra C M := ((algebraMap B M).comp C.subtype).toAlgebra
                  IsScalarTower C K M ∧ FiniteDimensional K M
